newsitem.title: USA: Wildfire near California coast spreads.
newsitem.headline: Wildfire near California coast spreads.

text.p: Firefighters lit backfires on Sunday to try to halt the advance of a big wildfire in California's scenic Los Padres National Forest, officials said.

The fire, which broke out Monday just south of Big Sur, a popular hiking and camping area on the central California coast, had consumed 9,500 acres of brush and forest by Sunday, Los Padres National Forest spokesman Joe Pasinato said.
The fire was 20 percent contained and there was no estimate of when it would be fully contained, he said. The blaze was burning towards the south and east.
The cause of the fire, 150 miles south of San Francisco, is suspected to be arson, officials said.
Pasinato said 2,267 firefighters battled the blaze, backed by 98 fire engines, 11 air tankers, 11 helicopters and 17 bulldozers.
He said firefighters were trying to halt the advance of the blaze, burning in steep, rugged terrain, by setting backfires that consume vegetation in the fire's path, starving it of fuel.
Firefighters had carried out "aggressive backburning operations on the southern perimeter" of the fire Sunday that had been successful, Pasinato said.
The fire has destroyed one home, nine outbuildings, two travel trailers and two vehicles, Pasinato said.
Fire enginers were in position to protect 43 homes near the fire, although there was no imminent danger to the houses, he said. Five firefighters have been injured battling the blaze, Pasinato said.
